title: Fisheries of the Northeastern United States; Summer Flounder Fishery; Quota Transfer From Massachusetts to Rhode Island
summary:
NOAA just made two mid-season adjustments for Northeast fisheries: Massachusetts is shifting a small portion of its 2025 summer flounder quota to Rhode Island, and the fall scup quota is getting a boost along with a higher per-trip landing limit.

The flounder change is modest—Massachusetts is moving 609 pounds to Rhode Island to square up landings made under a safe harbor situation. It’s a housekeeping step allowed under existing rules, and it slightly revises each state’s share through the end of the year. The scup change is bigger for the fall season. Because the fleet didn’t catch all of its January–April scup quota, the unused amount rolls into October–December. That pushes the fall quota higher and raises the per-trip limit from 12,000 to 15,000 pounds through December, then it returns to normal in January.

Who benefits? Rhode Island flounder boats get a small bump that matches what was already landed, keeping business moving without disruptions. Scup harvesters, dealers, and processors stand to gain from a larger fall quota and a higher trip limit, which can mean more efficient trips, steadier supply to markets, and potentially better planning for buyers and sellers. Consumers could see more local product available heading into the holidays.

Who might feel a pinch? Massachusetts flounder fishermen give up a minor amount of quota, though it’s tied to a specific safe harbor repayment and is unlikely to change overall operations. For scup, a higher trip limit can favor vessels with the capacity to land more fish at once, which may intensify competition and pressure prices for smaller operators. Conservation-minded readers may worry about late-season effort, but these moves are within the existing management plan and based on actual underharvest earlier in the year.

Overall, these adjustments aim to use available fish responsibly while keeping the fleet working and markets supplied as the year wraps up.
